 Mesa County continues counting ballots after Election Day 
 Mesa County continues counting ballots after Election Day By (Spence Breed) Updated : Nov. 4, 2026 at 7:39 PM MST GRAND JUNCTION, Colo. (KJCT) -Ballots are still being counted in Mesa County after Election Day, with 4,000 left to process as of Wednesday afternoon, Mesa County Clerk and Recorder Bobbie Gross said.
 Counting continues Wednesday
 Gross said election staff worked late into the night on the day of the election.
 “We ended the night at 3 a.m. We want to make sure that we’re processing them accurately. So at some point, my staff and our election judges are a little tired, so we gave them a little break to come back and we’re continuing the process this morning,” Gross said.
 All military and overseas ballots have eight days to arrive.
 Around 900 ballots need to be cured
 Mesa County also has around 900 ballots that need to be cured. Gross said those are ballots that the office needs to confirm the voter’s signature against the voter registration record.
 Voters whose ballots need to be cured can be notified in several ways.
 “We notify you by mail or e-mail if we have an e-mail on file. If you’re signed up for ballot track, you’ll also get that notification,” Gross said.
 Voters have several options to cure a ballot.
 “You can come into our office with the affidavit in your ID or you can do text secure, you can fax it and you can e-mail it over to us. We just have to have that within eight days of this election in order to make those ballots count,” Gross said.
 Recount possible in 3rd Congressional District
 The race for the 3rd Congressional District remains too close to call. If the count is close enough, it could trigger a recount.
 “It would be anybody that’s in that congressional district. So all those counties are in that congressional district. If it’s within 1/2 a percent, then it’s an automatic recount. And so all of us that are in that district would have to do the automatic recount,” Gross said.
 A recount also can happen if a candidate asks for one and covers the expenses.
 Mesa County says it will be a few weeks before results are official.
